{"file_path":"<path>","content":"# File type filtering

Type filtering lives in the `ignore` crate: `crates/ignore/src/types.rs` holds the
model and the matcher, `crates/ignore/src/default_types.rs` holds the shipped
definitions, and `crates/core/flags/hiargs.rs` turns the CLI flags into a
`Types` value. Everything below is behaviour of those three files.

## How definitions are represented

A definition is a `FileTypeDef { name: String, globs: Vec<String> }`. Nothing
more: a type is a name and a flat list of glob strings.

The defaults are a table, not a set of `FileTypeDef`s:

```rust
pub(crate) const DEFAULT_TYPES: &[(&[&str], &[&str])] = &[
    (&["py", "python"], &["*.py", "*.pyi"]),
```

The first slice is aliases and the second is globs. `TypesBuilder::add_defaults`
loops over every alias and adds every glob under it, so `py` and `python` become
two independent definitions that happen to carry identical globs. There's no
alias indirection at match time, and both names show up separately in
`--type-list`.

`TypesBuilder` accumulates two things: a `HashMap<String, FileTypeDef>` of
definitions and an ordered `Vec<Selection<()>>`, where `Selection` is either
`Select(name)` or `Negate(name)`. The map is unordered and the selection list
is positional. That split explains most of the behaviour you'll be asked about.

`add(name, glob)` appends to whatever definition already exists under `name`, so
repeated calls accumulate. It rejects the name `all`, and rejects any name that
isn't entirely alphanumeric, with `Error::InvalidDefinition`. That's why
`--type-add 'c++:*.cpp'` fails.

`add_def` parses the user-facing string form. `name:glob` calls `add`.
`name:include:a,b` checks that every listed type exists, then clones their globs
into `name`. The clone happens at call time, so include takes a snapshot: with
`--type-add 'src:include:rust' --type-add 'rust:*.foo'`, `src` doesn't get
`*.foo`. `clear(name)` removes the definition from the map outright.

## How the matcher is built

`TypesBuilder::build` walks the selections in order. For each one it looks the
name up in the definition map, erroring with `Error::UnrecognizedFileType` if
it's absent, and pushes every glob of that definition into a single
`GlobSetBuilder` with `literal_separator(true)`. Alongside, it records
`glob_to_selection: Vec<(usize, usize)>`, mapping each glob's index in the set
back to the selection it came from.

Because lookup happens in `build` rather than in `select`, selections resolve
against the *final* definition map. `rg -tfoo --type-add 'foo:*.foo'` works even
though the selection precedes the definition. Definition-mutating flags
(`--type-add`, `--type-clear`) do apply in command-line order relative to each
other, since `hiargs::types` replays one ordered `Vec<TypeChange>`.

`build` also sets `has_selected` if any selection is a `Select`, and allocates
`matches: Arc<Pool<Vec<usize>>>` as scratch space for match results.

## How matching works

`Types::matched(path, is_dir)` returns `Match<Glob>`:

- Directories and an empty glob set return `Match::None`. Type filters never
  prune traversal, so the walker still descends a directory named `dir.foo`
  under `-trust`.
- `pathutil::file_name` extracts the base name, and only that is matched. A
  definition glob containing `/` therefore matches nothing;
  `--type-add 'sub:src/*.rs' -tsub` lists no files. Keep default globs to base
  names.
- `GlobSet::matches_into` fills the pooled vec with matching indices in
  ascending order. The last one wins, and since indices are assigned in
  selection order, that means the last flag on the command line wins. A negated
  selection yields `Match::Ignore`, a selected one `Match::Whitelist`.
- With nothing matched, `has_selected` decides: `Match::Ignore(Glob::unmatched())`
  when at least one type was selected, otherwise `Match::None`. So `--type-not`
  on its own leaves unrelated files at `None` and lets ignore rules decide.

`Ignore::matched` in `dir.rs` consults overrides first, then ignore files, then
types, and an ignore result short-circuits. Types get the last word only among
whitelists.

## Changing this area

Adding a default type means one entry in `DEFAULT_TYPES`. The list is sorted by
first alias and the `default_types_are_sorted` test enforces it; the file header
asks for 79-column wrapping. Prefer base-name globs, and prefer adding an alias
to an existing entry over a second entry with the same globs.

Precedence is the part that's most often reported as a bug and isn't one. The
`matched!` tests at the bottom of `types.rs` pin it down: `matchnot4` selects
`rust`, negates `foo` (`*.{rs,foo}`), and expects `main.rs` to be ignored,
because the negation was listed second. Reverse the flags and the file matches.

Two more things worth checking before you change semantics. The module-level
docs in `types.rs` are doc tests and run under `cargo test -p ignore`, so they
pin the public API. And `Types` is cloned into the walker and stored as
`Arc<Types>` per directory, with the pooled match vec shared across threads, so
keep `matched` allocation-free.
"}

events.text:
Written to `DOCUMENT.md` (719 words). The repo tree is unchanged apart from the pre-existing modifications from the start of the session, and the temp scratch dir I used for verification is removed. `target/` was populated by the build, which is gitignored.

Sources read: `crates/ignore/src/types.rs`, `default_types.rs`, `pathutil.rs`, `dir.rs`, `crates/globset/src/lib.rs`, `crates/core/flags/hiargs.rs`, `crates/core/flags/defs.rs`, `crates/core/main.rs`.

Rather than infer behaviour from the code alone, I built `rg` and confirmed the non-obvious claims:

- **Selections resolve after all definitions.** `rg -tfoo --type-add 'foo:*.foo'` lists `a.foo`, because `build()` does the map lookup, not `select()`.
- **`include` snapshots.** `--type-add 'src2:include:rust' --type-add 'rust:*.foo'` does not put `*.foo` in `src2` — `add_def` clones the globs at call time.
- **Last flag wins.** `-trust --type-not foo` (with `foo:*.{rs,foo}`) lists nothing; reversing the two flags lists the `.rs` files. This is `glob_to_selection` plus the ascending sort in `GlobSet::matches_into`.
- **Base-name matching only.** `--type-add 'sub:src/*.rs' -tsub` matches nothing, since `Types::matched` passes only `file_name(path)` to the set.
- **Types never prune directories.** `-trust` still descends `dir.foo/` and finds `inner.rs`, because `matched` returns `Match::None` when `is_dir`.
- **A cleared-then-selected type is a build error**, not a silent no-op: `rg: unrecognized file type: rust`, exit 2.

Two judgment calls worth flagging: I left out a count of the shipped default types, since `--type-list` generates it and any number in prose goes stale; and I documented the three-way precedence in `Ignore::matched` (overrides, then ignore files, then types) only briefly, since it sits in `dir.rs` rather than in the type-filtering code proper.
